subject: VPC connectivity sales discovery - integration follow-up
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Samir Reddy <samir.reddy@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-24T15:12:00Z
Subject: Follow-up: VPC connectivity & integration next steps

Hi Samir / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the demo today - great convo. Per our discussion, I wanted to summarize the integration surface and next steps so your infra and security teams can review:

1) Integration goals (your checklist)
   - Route inference requests privately from your VPC to Redwood (private deployment / VPC endpoints)
   - Ensure only your app hosts can call the inference endpoints (IP allowlist + mTLS)
   - Preserve egress DNS resolution for model telemetry and optional autoscaling (we can proxy or use private DNS)
   - Support embeddings & reranker pipeline for search relevance (batching + structured output)

2) Technical options we recommend
   - VPC Endpoint (PrivateLink-style) to our regional ingress; no public internet egress required for inference traffic
   - IP allowlist at our edge + optional mutual TLS (mTLS) for client cert authentication for higher assurance
   - DNS: you can either use our DNS prefix (via private hosted zone) or forward queries through your resolver to preserve egress rules
   - Auth: API keys scoped to routes for dev/prod; for production we recommend short-lived certificates (mTLS) or OIDC + short-lived tokens (we support both)
   - Routing: route rules by path/model tag so you can split between cheaper quantized models and higher-accuracy variants

3) SDK / app integration notes
   - Our Node/Python SDKs support automatic retry, streaming, function/tool calling, and structured JSON output. Sample call: pass the `--auth=mTLS` flag or set REDWOOD_API_KEY as env var.
   - For embeddings + rerank, we suggest a two-step pipeline: client uploads documents to your embeddings store, call Redwood embeddings endpoint with batching (we support up to 10k tokens per batch), then call reranker endpoint with top-K context.

4) Next steps / owners
   - FinPay infra: share network diagram and allowed egress list (Samir) - due Tue 2027-06-29
   - Redwood infra (Jonas): will produce a one-page VPC endpoint connectivity patch and IP allowlist CIDR ranges by Thu 2027-06-26
   - Security sync (Marissa + Samir): quick 30-min call to confirm mTLS cert rotation & KMS options - propose Wed 2027-06-30 10:00 PT

I've attached a short integration guide and a suggested network diagram for your team to review. If you'd like, Jonas can join your infra call next week to walk through the endpoint setup.

Thanks -
Lauren
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Reddy <samir.reddy@finpay.com>

Cc: Priya Anand <priya.anand@finpay.com>
Date: 2027-06-25T09:34:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: VPC connectivity & integration next steps

Lauren -

Thanks for the clear summary. A couple of quick clarifications from our infra/security side after an internal review:

• For the VPC endpoint - do you support cross-account endpoints (we run infra in a shared services account and want the endpoint in a separate landing account)?
• For mTLS: we currently use an internal PKI. Can we bring our own client certs and rotate them?
• Egress/DNS: our policy blocks direct public DNS for service discovery; ideally we would forward DNS to our resolver. Is there any call Redwood makes to public services during inference (telemetry etc.) that would require extra egress permissions?

Also attaching our internal network diagram for context.

Samir
Head of Platform Engineering, FinPay
Attachment: finpay_network_diagram.png

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Samir Reddy <samir.reddy@finpay.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-26T14:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: VPC connectivity & integration next steps

Hey Samir -

Answers inline:

• Cross-account endpoints: yes, we support PrivateLink-style endpoints that can be configured for cross-account access. We'll provide the service name and IAM policy template for the endpoint consumer.

• Bring-your-own client certs: supported. You can upload CA chains (or trust anchors) to our control plane. We support cert rotation via a REST endpoint or automated ACME-style flow if you prefer.

• Egress / DNS: Our inference path does not contact external public services for model tokenization or scoring. Telemetry (optional) goes to our metrics/observability pipeline; if you want zero egress, we can disable telemetry for your account or route telemetry through your collector. For DNS, forwarding to your resolver works; we'll accept SRV/CNAME records or a private hosted zone depending on your preference.

Implementation notes / minimal required items for a dev proof-of-concept:
1) Provide an allowlist CIDR (or range) that will be allowed to call the PrivateLink endpoint. We'll provision the endpoint service name and the target ENIs.
2) Decide on auth mode for POC: API key scoped to a single model route (fastest) vs mTLS (slightly longer, but aligns with production security).
3) SDK setup: in your app container, install redwood-sdk v1.8+, set REDWOOD_API_KEY or mount client cert + key under /etc/redwood/mtls/ and set REDWOOD_AUTH_MODE=mTLS. We can share example docker-compose/k8s snippets.

If it helps, I can prepare a short runbook and the PrivateLink service name + example sg/route table changes tomorrow.

- Jonas
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
